questions.q: What does a physical backup actually capture, per this lesson?
options: The operating-system-level files — datafiles, control files, archived redo logs — at the block level
A SQL-describable export of tables and rows
Only the schema definitions, without any data
A screenshot of the database's current state
questions.explain: Physical backups, taken with RMAN, are block-level copies of the actual files Oracle stores data in.

questions.q: Why is a Data Pump dump file portable in a way a physical RMAN backup is not?
options: It's a logical description of objects and data, not a copy of specific datafiles tied to one database's exact version and platform
Data Pump dump files are smaller in size
RMAN backups can only be taken on Windows
Data Pump doesn't actually back up any data, only metadata
questions.explain: Because Data Pump exports a logical description rather than raw files, the dump can be imported into a different version or platform.

questions.q: Which tool would you use to restore an entire production database to an exact point in time, mid-transaction, after a bad batch job?
options: RMAN — restore physical files and apply redo for point-in-time recovery
Data Pump — impdp can replay transactions to an exact timestamp
Neither tool supports point-in-time recovery
TDE wallet recovery
questions.explain: Point-in-time recovery via applying redo is RMAN's domain; Data Pump has no redo-based recovery capability.

questions.q: A team needs to migrate just the HR schema from an on-prem Oracle 19c database to a cloud-hosted Oracle 21c database. Which approach fits?
options: Data Pump (expdp/impdp) — portable, schema-selective, version-independent
RMAN BACKUP DATABASE — restores the whole database including unrelated schemas
TDE wallet export
Neither tool can move data between Oracle versions
questions.explain: Data Pump's logical, portable dump format is exactly suited to schema-level, cross-version migrations.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a real production backup strategy uses both RMAN and Data Pump, rather than just one?
options: They solve different problems — RMAN for whole-database disaster recovery and point-in-time restore, Data Pump for migration and selective/portable exports
RMAN backups expire automatically and must be supplemented by Data Pump
Data Pump is strictly a faster version of RMAN
Using both is a legal requirement for Oracle licensing
questions.explain: The two tools are not interchangeable; each is the right tool for a different class of requirement.
